verdictStatement: All four claimed honesty repairs are genuine and I verified each against primary bytes, including reaching into git history to confirm what v2 actually did rather than accepting v3's account of it. The closed roster holds exactly: a full recursive diff finds 32 differing paths and every one is named. Every substantive block — truthTables, permissionVocabulary, linearization, raceSemantics, refusalFamilies, fixture classes, coverageObligation, the ENFORCED census, whatThisDoesNotDo — is byte-identical to the D-042-accepted candidate, so the 'changing a truth-table ENFORCED cell' attack fails by measurement rather than by argument. What withholds acceptance is one residue of the very class this generation exists to repair. PT2-CX-A1 asked for inherited content to be separated from live content, and v3 does that thoroughly for the COORD and file-08 pins — flagging them measuredAtV2Authoring, adding an inheritedV2Pins block, and rewriting recordedInputs.discipline to withdraw v2's blanket this-authoring claim. The one inherited block it left unlabeled is the top-level predecessor block, which still names v1 as this artifact's predecessor while basedOn names v2.

Because linearization and the fixture classes are unchanged from v2, any bad attribution at the original sites would have survived the repair, so I enumerated every site in the artifact containing either string — eight of them — and read each. Not one attributes the coinage to file 03. caseBefore is careful in the other direction, saying file 03's clause 'names the ordering, not the ICO value'. ID-DEP-P14 says file 03 names 'the ordering and the COMPLETED disclosure only' and that no owner other than the DR-105 row has ratified the two strings. FX-6 presents itself as a wording golden over this contract's vocabulary. The attack does not land at any of the eight.

advisories.title: The register-row refresh is selective, and its completeness rests on four cells the roster did not touch
advisories.detail: v3 adds rowVerbatim, which carries the whole live row, alongside the pre-existing parsed cells decision, owner, sourcePin, acceptanceEvidence and consequence. The roster names source, status, sliceScoping, locationDiscipline, rowVerbatim and v2CarriedAt — the four parsed content cells are not on it and are unchanged from v2, i.e. they were parsed from the superseded f0d72536 row. I checked all four against the live row's cells and every one matches exactly, so the carry is complete today. But that is because those cells happen not to have moved between f0d72536 and 1cdcf9d4; only the status cell did. The row is now stored twice, whole and parsed, with only one of the two representations on the refresh roster.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: Nothing is wrong at these bytes — I verified the agreement rather than assuming it, and the artifact's own reviewGuidance supplies a re-read hook for the status cell. This is a drift surface for the next generation, not a defect in this one.
advisories.suggestedFix: Either derive the parsed cells from rowVerbatim, or put all of /registerRowCarriedWhole on the roster whenever the row is refreshed, so a future status-cell-only change cannot leave the parsed half behind.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed: That a truth-table ENFORCED cell moved under cover of honesty work. Structural equality refutes it: truthTables and enforcedColumnCensus are identical to the D-042-accepted bytes.
That the two-way minted-or-reserved rule survives somewhere outside the repaired sliceScoping field. A whole-document regex sweep returns zero occurrences of any two-way formulation.
That a linearization or fixture site still sources the coined disclosure strings to file 03. All eight sites enumerated and read; none does, and caseBefore explicitly disclaims it.
That T-6 overstates file 03's silence. Grep over docs/v2/architecture/ returns zero occurrences of either coined string, and the quoted file-03 sentence is verbatim.
That v3's account of v2's stale carry is itself unverified. I located the f0d72536 blob in git history and confirmed line 268 and the abbreviated 'OPEN' status.
That the inherited-versus-live split is cosmetic. The two inherited pins have genuinely moved and the three unmoved ones are correctly claimed as still matching; the labels are load-bearing.

That the working-tree modification of host-effect-authorization.v8.json lets the artifact claim more than D-093 recorded. The artifact names that exact hazard and pins the committed digest, which I confirmed.
That some path changed outside the closed roster. All 32 differing paths are named, including the three the roster identifies by element rather than by key.
coordinatorNote: This is careful work and the verification was mostly a matter of trying to catch it out and failing. Two things are worth the coordinator's attention beyond the verdict. First, the honesty repairs are verifiable in both directions: v3 does not merely assert that v2's register-row carry was stale, it records where and how, and I confirmed that at the historical blob. Second, the artifact anticipates the one trap in its own environment — the working-tree modification of the host-effect file — and rules it out as this-authoring evidence before a reviewer can be misled by it. The single SHOULD-FIX is the last unlabeled inherited block in a generation whose purpose is labelling inherited blocks, and it is a rename. The advisory is a drift surface for the next successor, not a defect here. DR-105 remains OPEN, the subject remains CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED / DO-NOT-SEAL / binds NOTHING, FC-C1 is not treated as recorded, host-effect is not applied, and nothing in this verdict marks the row SATISFIED or authorizes docs/v2/implementation/.
